_why: Stack 4 of authored rows (ticket the-domain-carries-the-inference-side, idea 2026-08-08-now-there-was-supposed-to-be-a): the DOMAIN VERTICALS — the second part of the inference proxy. A row answers WITH WHAT CONTENT a request arrives (prompts), and HOW it may be gotten (escalation walk-rule, model preference); the reasoning stays in the calling device — Akien's boundary sentence: 'the reasoning happens in the calling device, but getting the inference comes from here.' Rows are FIELD SETS an instance composes, never classes it belongs to (the ticket/probe/task precedent; falsifier tell 6). Exactly one row is default: a bare call rides it silently, and the default being a ROW keeps it out of code branches. Prompts dress the request on the MISS path only — a stored answer is never transformed on the way out (Law 7) — and the dressed form is what canonicalizes, so editing a row's prompt text is asking a new question, never serving a stale answer to it.
escalation_note: escalation.allow, when present, lists the provider names the routed walk may dial for this domain — a GETTING rule (which rungs, never a judgment on answer content). Absent means every survivor of the nest's shake, which is today's walk exactly.
prefers_note: prefers lists model names the nest ORDERS toward, never a cut: survivors carrying a preferred model sort ahead, cost order kept within each group, and every sieve's cut is untouchable by preference. Empty means the cheapest-first order stands untouched.

domains.name: general
domains.why: the default vertical: a bare call is a general call, and general adds NOTHING by design — empty prompts, no walk restriction, no preference — so the default lives as an authored row, not a code branch, and a pre-domains caller is byte-for-byte unchanged.

domains.name: coding
domains.why: code-shaped asks want models tuned for code and answers that run — the vertical the future fail-over-to-LLM inspectors ride (their tickets cast when the consumer appears, per the idea).

prompts.generate: You are assisting with software engineering inside the Cairn system. Answer with precise, runnable code, name concrete files and commands, and say plainly when you are unsure.

domains.name: research
domains.why: the librarian's vertical — the first real consumer (Telos 2): a research turn wants answers grounded in the provided material, with gaps named rather than papered over. Declared by the librarian's seam, never inferred from message content (chat tooth 15).

prompts.generate: You are assisting with research. Ground your answer in the material provided, cite what you actually use, and say plainly when the material does not answer the question.

domains.name: builder-aider
domains.why: the offload vertical: the aider shim's build traffic, pinned to a local model on a local box and FENCED there. The pin and the fence are the whole row — escalation.allow ['hex'] means this domain's traffic can never walk out to a paid provider, so an unattended builder that loops cannot spend money it was never authorised to spend. Empty prompts are deliberate and are this row's clearest statement of the boundary sentence: aider composes its own instructions, and getting the inference is all that comes from here. A chat request is undressed by construction anyway (the seam dresses generate only), so writing prompts here would be text nothing reads.
